citations.text: OpenEvo comparison of Pillow (2012), Barzilai and Chinn (2018, 2024) and Hanisch and Eirdosh (2023), 2026-11-18. A shared field concept proposed by the comparison; no source defines it.
Barzilai, S., & Chinn, C. A. (2024). The AIR and Apt-AIR frameworks of epistemic performance and growth: Reflections on educational theory development. Educational Psychology Review, 36(3), 91.
Hanisch, S., & Eirdosh, D. (2023). Behavioral science and education for sustainable development: Towards metacognitive competency. Sustainability, 15(9), 7413.

en.general: Carrying an understanding or a way of performing into a new task, subject or situation, and adjusting it to fit. The Hanisch and Eirdosh paper treats transfer as a design goal supported by an underlying competency. Barzilai and Chinn treat adaptivity to task and discipline as one of five aspects of apt performance.

examples: Using a payoff matrix from a lesson on cooperation to explain a different social dilemma.
Students choosing different criteria for a descriptive model than for an explanatory one.
nonExamples: Repeating a worked example on the same task.
Applying a rule everywhere without checking the fit.
